Why can't people find my business on Google?

2026-08-19 · 3 min read

Nine times out of ten it is not the website's fault, and the fix costs nothing. The most common reason a local business is invisible on Google is that it has no Google Business Profile — the free listing that puts you on the map with your hours, your photos and a call button.

You have no Google Business Profile

When somebody searches for a barber, a mechanic or a nail salon nearby, Google shows a map with three businesses above everything else. Those three come from Business Profiles, not from websites. If you do not have one, you cannot appear there at all — no matter how good your site is.

Creating one is free and takes about twenty minutes. Google then posts a card to your address with a code to confirm you are really there. That verification is the part people give up on, and it is the part that matters.

You have almost no reviews

Between two businesses at the same distance, Google shows the one with more reviews. It is the single strongest lever a local business has, and it is the one thing a competitor cannot copy from you overnight.

Ask every customer, not only the happy ones. Filtering — asking for a review only when someone seems pleased — breaks Google's rules and can get your reviews removed. A message an hour after the visit, or a QR code at the till, is enough.

Your details disagree with each other

Your name, address and phone number appear on your site, on Facebook, in directories. If they differ — an old phone number here, an abbreviated street there — Google becomes less sure the business is real, and less sure businesses rank lower.

Write the three down once, exactly as they should appear, and make every place match, character for character.

Your site never says where you are

A surprising number of small business sites never name their own city. The page says "we do great haircuts" and nothing else. Google has to guess who to show it to, and when it guesses it guesses conservatively.

Your city belongs in the page title, in the first heading and in the footer with the full address. That is not keyword stuffing — it is answering the question the searcher actually asked, which was "near me".

Your site is new, and that is normal

A new site takes weeks to be indexed and months to rank for anything competitive. This is the one item on this list where the answer is patience rather than action.

What you can do is stop waiting passively: submit the site in Google Search Console, and lean on the Business Profile in the meantime, because the map results move far faster than the blue links below them.

So what should you do first?

Claim and verify the Business Profile. It is free, it takes an afternoon, and for most local businesses it changes more than anything else on this list. Then start collecting reviews, and only then worry about the website.

Anyone telling you that a website alone will get you found is selling you the second step and skipping the first.
